nodes.label: README.md — SmartOps architecture, tech stack, architectural considerations
SmartOps AI Observability Platform
nodes.rationale: Full-stack AI-powered observability platform built as a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (apps/api, apps/web, apps/ai-agents, packages/shared-types, infra, e2e). It unifies metrics, logs and traces in one dashboard and uses Mastra AI agents to detect anomalies, run RCA and auto-create ServiceNow tickets behind a human-in-the-loop gate. Framing goal: compress the on-call investigation loop from ~20 minutes of manual correlation across Grafana/Kibana/Jaeger/runbooks down to ~30 seconds.

nodes.label: VictoriaMetrics (time-series metric store, :8428)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Prometheus as the single time-series source of truth: identical PromQL API so existing Grafana dashboards migrate at zero cost, 10-40x better storage compression, no cardinality explosion at scale, single binary with no sidecar and no pushgateway needed for short-lived jobs. Both the SmartOps anomaly detector and Grafana read the same PromQL endpoint, so there is no ETL, no sync and no divergence between what an operator sees in Grafana and what the AI analyzed — which matters for incident retrospectives. Production upgrade path is VictoriaMetrics Cluster (vminsert/vmselect/vmstorage) for >100k samples/s or HA; on AWS it is swappable for Amazon Managed Prometheus since it sits behind an interface.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch 8 (logs, metrics, traces store, :9200)
nodes.rationale: Holds OTel ECS-mapped logs (smartops-logs), Kafka-sourced metrics (smartops-metrics-*) and distributed trace spans (smartops-traces-*). The RCA agent searches it for error logs and slow/errored spans in the anomaly region + time window. Access is wrapped in withFallback() so an ES outage degrades RCA confidence instead of failing the workflow. Production: dedicated cluster with 3 master / 2 data / 2 coordinating replicas plus ILM hot-warm-cold-delete tiers; swappable for OpenSearch on AWS.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Collector (OTLP gRPC :4317 / HTTP :4318)
nodes.rationale: Ingests OTLP from the simulator and maps logs to ECS fields before writing to Elasticsearch; its docker_stats receiver scrapes SmartOps's own container metrics (replaceable with kubeletstats in K8s). Acknowledged gap: agent.generate() calls are not yet wrapped in OTel spans, so the AI layer itself is a black box while the infrastructure it watches is fully observed.

nodes.label: Fastify 4 API (:3000) — REST routes, RBAC, SSE
nodes.rationale: Stateless (JWT auth, no in-process session) so it scales horizontally via replicaCount or CPU-based HPA. Hosts REST routes with Swagger, the SSE /metrics/stream endpoint, Drizzle ORM access to PostgreSQL, and imports @smartops/ai-agents in-process. Trade-off: running Mastra inside the Fastify process risks blocking the event loop on CPU-intensive workflows — a separate Mastra server process is the production upgrade path.

nodes.label: Next.js 14 web dashboard (:3001)
nodes.rationale: App Router + Tailwind + Recharts + SWR. Surfaces the live dashboard (SSE consumer), AI Insights, assets and alert rules, and the incident approval modal. Stateless, scales freely.

nodes.label: @smartops/ai-agents — four Mastra agents (anomalyDetector, rootCauseAnalyzer, forecastingAgent, servicenowAgent)
nodes.rationale: Lives as an independent pnpm workspace package rather than inside the API's src/ so any future consumer (CLI, Slack bot, worker process) can import it without pulling in Fastify, and so agent tests run without an HTTP server. The package boundary also enforces discipline: the API can only call exported functions (detectAnomalies, analyzeRootCause, the Mastra instance) and cannot reach into Mastra internals. Model split is cost-driven: claude-haiku-4-5 for detection/forecasting/ServiceNow structuring, claude-sonnet-4-6 for RCA narrative. Agents are stateless, so multiple API instances can invoke them safely.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop approval gate (await-approval step)
nodes.rationale: Enforced as a structural guarantee at the Mastra execution model level, not as a UI convention or an if (autoApprove) flag that could drift or be misconfigured. suspend() throws internally to halt the step — it is not a conditional return — so there is no code path that creates a ServiceNow ticket without a human calling /resume. RBAC reinforces it: only operator and admin roles can trigger RCA or approve; viewers cannot. The AI reads telemetry and produces a hypothesis but touches nothing in production.

nodes.label: Deterministic z-score anomaly detection (detectAnomalies)
nodes.rationale: Pure statistical math with no LLM call: 12 parallel scans (4 metrics x 3 regions) compute a z-score against a 10-minute baseline, flagged when z > 2 AND the value clears a warning floor. Chosen over an ML model because there is no training data, no model drift, and every firing is auditable down to mean/stddev/z-score. Deterministic detection runs before probabilistic reasoning so the healthy path costs zero AI spend and sub-second latency. The threshold is deliberately conservative — lowering it to cut false negatives would push RCA work onto every minor fluctuation, compounding cost and alert fatigue. An absolute backstop (always flag CPU >= 85%) covers the cold-start case where there is not enough baseline for a meaningful z-score.

nodes.label: ServiceNow incident creation (servicenowAgent)
nodes.rationale: Final workflow step: structures RCA output into a ServiceNow incident payload and creates the ticket over REST, returning a SNOW ticket ID that is written back onto the PostgreSQL incident row. Reachable only after a human approval resumes the workflow.

nodes.label: Anthropic Claude via @ai-sdk/anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5)
nodes.rationale: Integrates directly with Mastra so model swaps (Haiku <-> Sonnet) are one-line per agent. Sonnet handles the RCA narrative where reasoning quality matters; Haiku handles detection reasoning, forecasting and ServiceNow payload structuring where speed and cost dominate. The LLM only runs after a deterministic anomaly is already confirmed.

nodes.label: Turborepo build orchestration
nodes.rationale: Drives dev/build/typecheck/lint across all workspace packages in the monorepo.

nodes.label: pnpm workspaces monorepo layout
nodes.rationale: apps/ (api, web, ai-agents), packages/ (shared-types), infra/, e2e/. The workspace boundary is what lets @smartops/ai-agents be consumed independently of Fastify and lets Zod schemas and TS types be shared between api and web.

nodes.label: Kafka fan-out pipeline (one producer, two consumer groups)
nodes.rationale: simulate-infra.ts publishes a MetricMessage to smartops.metrics every 5s per region; consumer group smartops-vm-writer remote-writes to VictoriaMetrics and smartops-es-writer bulk-indexes to Elasticsearch (50 docs/flush). The groups are independent — stopping one does not affect the other, and neither knows the other exists — so adding a third sink is a new consumer file with zero producer change. This decoupling is the platform's stated scaling story.

nodes.label: MetricMessage contract (producer ↔ consumers)
nodes.rationale: Currently a TypeScript interface shared by convention — enforced at compile time but not at runtime, so nothing catches a breaking schema change before it reaches consumers. Named as the number-one thing to do differently.

nodes.label: Kafka Schema Registry (planned production upgrade)
nodes.rationale: Confluent or Redpanda with Avro/Protobuf would enforce the MetricMessage contract at runtime, catch breaking changes before consumers see them, and enable schema evolution without coordinated deploys. Explicitly listed as 'what I'd do differently — from day one'.

nodes.label: Dead-letter topic smartops.metrics.dlq (planned)
nodes.rationale: Both Kafka consumers currently re-queue silently on ES/VM errors. A DLQ would capture failed messages for inspection and replay without blocking the main consumer group — standard production Kafka practice.

nodes.label: preDetectedAnomaly pass-through (race-condition fix)
nodes.rationale: Simulated CPU spikes last only 25 seconds, so re-running detectAnomalies() inside the workflow after the user clicks 'Trigger RCA' would often find the spike already resolved and silently return 'no anomaly found'. detectAnomalyStep therefore accepts an optional preDetectedAnomaly and returns immediately without querying VictoriaMetrics — the anomaly captured at scan time is the anomaly analyzed. The pattern generalises: any trigger source (webhook, CLI, alert rule) can inject a pre-validated anomaly event and skip re-detection.

nodes.label: withFallback() graceful degradation
nodes.rationale: Elasticsearch and trace-fetch calls race against a 5-second timeout and catch both immediate errors (connection refused) and hangs. If ES is down the RCA agent receives empty log/trace results and writes a lower-confidence, metrics-only analysis rather than failing the workflow. Deliberate trade-off: some incidents get incomplete RCA when a data source is unavailable, but the pipeline stays running and the confidence score communicates the data-quality gap honestly.

nodes.label: simulate-infra.ts — infrastructure metric/log/trace simulator
nodes.rationale: Publishes JSON MetricMessage events to Kafka every 5s per region, pushes OTLP logs to the collector, and bulk-indexes distributed trace spans into smartops-traces-{date} every 10s. During an injected CPU anomaly the affected region's spans shift to a 35% error rate and 300ms-5s latency so the trace evidence correlates with the anomaly window and drives the RCA confidence score upward. Needs ~2 minutes of baseline before z-score detection is meaningful.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM (PostgreSQL access + migrations)
nodes.rationale: Backs the API's PostgreSQL access with generated migrations (pnpm db:generate / db:migrate); its client pool is configured via DATABASE_URL, and PgBouncer requires ?pgbouncer=true to disable prepared statements.

nodes.label: @smartops/shared-types (Zod schemas + TypeScript types)
nodes.rationale: Single source of contract shared across api and web; Zod also validates Mastra workflow inputData/resumeData shapes at compile time.

nodes.label: Un-instrumented AI layer (planned OTel spans around agent.generate())
nodes.rationale: The platform observes infrastructure thoroughly but the AI layer itself is a black box. Wrapping each agent.generate() call in an OTel span would surface LLM latency, tool-call counts and retries — closing what the author calls an obvious irony.

nodes.label: Playwright E2E suite (e2e/)
nodes.rationale: Covers auth, dashboard, assets and AI agent flows end to end.
